---
engine: markdown
title: "Structured data (YAML, TOML, XML, RDS, FWF)"
---

These formats are read into a data frame with one row per record. Nested
structures are kept when the output format supports nesting (JSON, YAML,
TOML, XML, RDS), and flattened otherwise.

## YAML

Files ending in `.yaml` or `.yml` are read and written with
[yaml](https://cran.r-project.org/package=yaml). A list of records becomes a
data frame:

```{term}
echo "- name: web
  port: 8080
  replicas: 3
- name: db
  port: 5432
  replicas: 1" > servers.yaml
rush run 'df' servers.yaml
```

Write YAML with `-O yaml` or an output file ending in `.yaml`. Converting
nested JSON keeps the nesting:

```{term}
echo '[{"name": "web", "limits": {"cpu": 2, "memory": "4G"}},
       {"name": "db", "limits": {"cpu": 4, "memory": "16G"}}]' > limits.json
rush convert -O yaml limits.json
```

## TOML

Files ending in `.toml` are read with
[RcppTOML](https://cran.r-project.org/package=RcppTOML). Each record is
written as a table in an array named after `--output-record` (`record` by
default):

```{term}
rush convert --output-record server -o servers.toml servers.yaml
cat servers.toml
```

Reading TOML sorts the columns by name:

```{term}
rush run 'df' servers.toml
```

## XML

Files ending in `.xml` are read and written with
[xml2](https://xml2.r-lib.org/). Each row becomes an element, with a child
element per column. Use `--output-root` and `--output-record` to name the
elements (`root` and `record` by default):

```{term}
rush convert --output-root servers --output-record server -o servers.xml \
  servers.yaml
cat servers.xml
```

XML has no column types, so every column is read as text:

```{term}
rush run 'df' servers.xml
```

## RDS

R's own serialization format. Files ending in `.rds` are read and written with
`readr::read_rds()` and `readr::write_rds()`. Unlike CSV, RDS keeps R's column
types, such as factors and dates:

```{term}
rush run -o flowers.rds 'head(iris, 3)'
rush run 'tibble::tibble(column = names(df), class = sapply(df, class))' \
  flowers.rds
```

## Fixed-width files (FWF)

Files ending in `.fwf` are read with `readr::read_fwf()`, which detects the
column positions from the spaces between them. Such files rarely have a
header, so name the columns with `--names`:

```{term}
echo "Alice   30 Amsterdam
Bob     25 Rotterdam
Carol   35 Utrecht" > people.fwf
rush run --names name,age,city 'df' people.fwf
```

Use `-F fwf` for files with another extension, such as `.txt`. Fixed-width
files can only be read.

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f servers.yaml limits.json servers.toml servers.xml flowers.rds people.fwf
```
